Consequences of Inactivity in Judicial Terms for Inheritance Acceptance In an inheritance division regarding a property in Castelsardo, several potential heirs were summoned under Art. 481 c.c. to declare their acceptance within a judicial deadline. The legal issue concerns the evidentiary and substantive weight of a called heir's silence within a "termino di decadenza". The interpretative challenge was whether non-appearance could be equated to a specific legal status. The Court applied the principle that failure to appear and declare acceptance within the court-ordered term is equivalent to a formal renunciation of the inheritance, effectively excluding those individuals from the succession.
Judicial Assignment of Property to the Majority Shareholder The plaintiff, who had acquired a 1/4 share from a co-heir via a private deed and already held a significant portion of the estate, requested the full attribution of the property. This involves the legal classification of "assegnazione" under Art. 720 c.c. and the validity of private transfers within a division lawsuit. The interpretative problem arises when the property is not conveniently divisible and shares have been traded privately. The Court ruled that since the private deed was legally recognized and the property met urban planning requirements, the asset could be entirely attributed to the majority shareholder, especially as cash equalizations had already been paid and acknowledged.
